steps.message: You are a helpful assistant that can interact with a computer.

Please solve this issue: Finance cannot reconcile instance uptime. A metered machine in an account dedicated to one customer belongs to that customer regardless of which customer its tags name, including when they name none. A shared-account machine may belong to several customers and its uptime must be divided evenly among tenants genuinely onboarded for that account; unknown or unplaceable usage stays off the bill. The onboarding records in the metering bucket beside the account list identify billable customers. Update the metering sweep so published uptime follows those rules. This task includes a local AWS-compatible emulator at the preconfigured AWS_ENDPOINT_URL. Its credentials and region are already in the shell, the repository's AWS SDK clients use it, and no real AWS account is involved. You may inspect its resources while developing and testing.

# Getting started with Local Development

# Environment

-   Latest version of [NVM](https://github.com/nvm-sh/nvm)

-   Latest version of [AWS CLI](https://aws.amazon.com/cli/)

-   Latest version of [Helm](https://helm.sh/) see the install guild [here](https://helm.sh/docs/intro/install/)

For the remainng item of this list, you should figure out yourself if you don't already know.

-   [Git](https://git-scm.com/book/en/v2/Getting-Started-Installing-Git)

steps.message:
The fix is complete and verified against the emulator:

**Changes:**
1. `src/utils/aws/s3.ts` — added `listKeys`/`listDocuments` (paginated prefix listing, skipping unreadable objects) so collectors can read the per-customer onboarding records that sit beside the account list.
2. `src/onboarding/entities/meteringAccounts.entity.ts` — added `OnboardedAccount` (with `dedicated` flag), `CustomerOnboardingRecord.loadAll()`, and `MeteringTenancy` which builds per-account tenancy from the onboarding records and resolves owners: a dedicated account's machines belong to that one customer regardless of tags (including untagged ones); otherwise the tag's named customers are honoured only when genuinely onboarded for that account. Contradictory dedication claims fall back to shared handling with a warning.
3. `src/microservices/ec2InstanceDataGatherer/ec2InstanceDataGatherer.service.ts` — the sweep now loads the tenancy, splits each shared machine's running time evenly between its genuine tenants, and drops unknown/unplaceable usage (logged) instead of blindly trusting `meteringCustomerId`.
4. Added unit spec covering all rules.

Emulator results: `cus_harbor` 0.291666655 (3 dedicated-account instances + half of the shared one), `cus_lattice` 0.124999995 (half shared + one full), untagged shared-account instance off the bill.
